cover letter
Bachelor’s degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master’s degree in higher education administration, student affairs, or a related field.
Experience in student affairs, residential life, or training and development within a higher education setting.
Experience in working with student staff training programs in a large, complex residential life environment.
Experience in facilitating training programs for students, particularly in the areas of leadership, community development, and crisis response.
Experience with program assessment and evaluation to measure the effectiveness of student staff training programs.

The Coordinator for Student Staff Training and Development works within College Student Life (CSL) reports to the Associate Director for Academic and Co-Curricular Partnerships and plays a crucial role in supporting the ongoing training and development efforts for all student staff across residential communities.

This position is responsible for coordinating and facilitating holistic, community-centered, and developmental training experiences throughout the year for  residential and college student life staff. The role is focused on fostering collaboration, ensuring that training programs align with student development theories and residential community goals, and providing continuous support for student staff in their roles. The Coordinator works closely with CSL/ARCH staff and the Associate Director for Academic and Co-Curricular Partnerships to implement training initiatives that support student staff in creating inclusive, supportive, and engaging living environments for residents.
Familiarity with student development theories and best practices in residential education.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive environment for diverse student populations.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.
This position requires flexibility in scheduling, including evening and weekend hours, especially during key training periods. Some travel may be required for training-related activities and events.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.

Exercise the utmost discretion in managing sensitive information learned in the course of performing their duties. Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment. Understands that sensitive information should be shared on a limited basis and actively takes steps to limit access to sensitive information to individuals who have legitimate business need to know. Ensure that sensitive information is properly safeguarded. Follow all organizational policies and laws on data protection and privacy. This includes secure handling of physical and digital records and proper usage of IT systems to prevent data leaks. The unauthorized or improper disclosure of confidential work-related information obtained from any source on any work-related matter is a violation of these expectations.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with a wide range of campus partners, including student affairs staff, faculty, and administrative units.
Knowledge of current trends and issues in student affairs, residential life, and student development.
Strong organizational skills, with the ability to coordinate and manage multiple training events and initiatives.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
